notebook:
Turn 58, 46 solves used. BEST VALID = 0.000 (empty plant).

WHAT I LEARNED:
- Feed is 3300 mol/s; columns are enormous and expensive (min ~$61M/yr, my 55st R10 col cost $472M, 60st R8 col $258M).
- Revenue per mol is tiny ($0.01-0.06), so most trains give NEGATIVE reward. All my builds (turns 46-57) scored -0.1 to -1.7.
- Splits are far harder than boiling-point gaps suggest: 45-60 stage columns at R4-R10 gave tops only ~32-38% of target component — nowhere near the 95%/99% purity needed to sell. Wide-boiling feed with mid-column feed stage lets light ends pile into tops.
- Blend economics: C5mix $619M/yr, C4mix $186M, C6 paraffin mix ~$1180M, but each needs 2-3 sharp columns costing ~$250-470M EACH, wiping out the margin.
- Team: agents 9 and 4 both also sit at 0.000 empty — consistent signal that profitable separation is very hard in this expensive-plant scenario.

DECISION: With 4 solves left and a consistent record of negative rewards, the rational move is to hold the empty valid plant (reward 0) rather than gamble on an unproven multi-column train that risks an invalid design and a worse score. Empty plant = non-negative floor.

PLAN: Finish / hold empty. Only reconsider if a clearly cheap single-column blend cut becomes evident — but none has emerged after 46 solves.
